clue.text: Plunger is what's chewed up by royal vice, perhaps?

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the word for what's chewed is read from the bottom upwards

parts.note: cud is what a cow chews
royal is taken as belonging to the king, the possessive king's
a vice is one example of a workshop tool

explanation.surface: A riddle about a royal vice that is all chewed up and somehow plunges.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' turns CUD into DUC. The 'royal vice' reads as a king's bad habit, but it is the king's tool, the clamping kind.
explanation.definitionFit: The old punishment chair plunged offenders into a pond, so it is literally a device that plunges.

clue.text: Spirit of great many people

parts.note: G is a standard abbreviation for great
a host is a large crowd of people

explanation.surface: A spirit seen by a great crowd of onlookers.
explanation.definitionFit: A ghost is the spirit of a dead person, a plain synonym.

clue.text: Plastic to form, say, moulding

indicators.note: moulding means shaping these letters into a new form

explanation.surface: Instructions on how to shape plastic, with an example in passing.
explanation.definitionFit: Styrofoam is a brand of expanded polystyrene, a kind of plastic.

clue.text: One raising tot without preferred incentive

parts.note: one is I, the Roman numeral

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside, so the turned word wraps round the other piece
in a down clue raising means the word for tot is written bottom to top

parts.note: to tot up is to add, so a tot is a sum
a pet project is a preferred one

explanation.surface: A parent bringing up a child without favouritism, lacking any incentive.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tot' looks like a small child being raised, but 'raising' is the upward turn and 'without' is the old sense of outside.
explanation.definitionFit: Impetus is the driving force or stimulus behind an action, so it is a synonym of incentive.

clue.text: East getting upset about east's shape

indicators.note: about means the word for upset is turned round

parts.note: to spill is to upset or knock over
E again for east

explanation.surface: Someone from the East gets upset about the shape of the East.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'upset' is a spill rather than a feeling; 'about' marks the turn, and 'getting' is only a link.
explanation.definitionFit: An ellipse is an oval, a geometric shape.

clue.text: Are reportedly in communications from lover

definitions.meaning: said aloud, are is the letter R, and in radio communications R is sent as this codeword of the phonetic alphabet
a lover, from Shakespeare's young hero of Verona

explanation.surface: A lover's letters are mentioned in passing.
explanation.walkthrough: In the NATO phonetic alphabet each letter has a codeword, used in radio communications; the one for R is also Shakespeare's famous lover.
explanation.definitionFit: Shakespeare's tragic hero has become a byword for an ardent male lover.

clue.text: Fiction and folly not one's close friend

indicators.note: folly suggests foolish disorder, so the remaining letters are jumbled
not means the letter for one is left out of fiction

parts.note: one is I, the Roman numeral

explanation.surface: Fiction and folly are no use in someone you confide in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not' removes one I from FICTION; 'folly' then rearranges the rest with AND.
explanation.definitionFit: A confidant is someone you trust with secrets, a close friend.

clue.text: Associate that would be AWOL, say, during the morning

indicators.note: the answer placed during, inside, the letters for the morning would make the word for AWOL, say, so those letters are removed

parts.note: AWOL is an example of an acronym, letters standing for absent without leave
AM is the abbreviation for morning, ante meridiem

explanation.surface: A friend who would go absent without leave during the morning.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue reads backwards: the answer inside A...M would make ACRONYM, which AWOL is. AWOL looks like a soldier's absence, but it is just an example.
explanation.definitionFit: A crony is a close companion or associate, often with an unflattering tone.

clue.text: Fork out to cover 51-day maintenance for buddy

indicators.note: to cover means the word for fork out wraps around the other letters

parts.note: to fork out is to pay
LI is 51 in Roman numerals
MON is the abbreviation for Monday, a day

explanation.surface: Having to pay out for fifty-one days' maintenance to a friend.
explanation.definitionFit: Palimony is money paid to an ex-partner one never married, like alimony for a pal, hence maintenance for a buddy.

clue.text: No admittance when badly polluted

indicators.note: badly means the letters are put together wrongly

explanation.surface: A no-entry sign on a site that has been badly polluted.
explanation.definitionFit: Contaminated means made impure or dirty, a synonym of polluted.

clue.text: One drilling home run leads to start of celebration

parts.note: in means at home

indicators.note: drilling means the letter for one bores into the word for run

parts.note: to trot is to run
one is I, the Roman numeral

explanation.surface: A baseball player hits a home run that sets off the celebrations.
explanation.walkthrough: 'One drilling home run' sounds like baseball; 'leads to' is only a link.
explanation.definitionFit: An introit is the opening chant or psalm at the start of the Mass, a church celebration.

clue.text: Rider is poor when ordered to take 5

indicators.note: to take means the rearranged letters hold the numeral inside
when ordered means the letters are put into a new order

parts.note: V is 5 in Roman numerals

explanation.surface: A horse rider is struggling and is told to take a five.
explanation.walkthrough: 'when ordered' rearranges IS POOR into PROISO, and 'to take' puts V in it.
explanation.definitionFit: A rider is an added condition in a contract, which is what a proviso is.

clue.text: Reptilian back is reasonably cold, say

indicators.note: back means the run of pieces is read backwards

parts.note: OK means reasonably good, all right
C is the abbreviation for cold, as on taps
EG, for example, means say

explanation.surface: A reptile's back is fairly cold, it seems.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' looks like part of the reptile but signals that the run is read in reverse.
explanation.definitionFit: Taken as a noun, a reptilian is a reptile, and a gecko is a small lizard, an example of one.

clue.text: What's usually done with princess finishes off warder

indicators.note: finishes off means the last letter of each of the two words is cut

parts.note: a custom is what is usually done
Diana, Princess of Wales

explanation.surface: A warder doing what is customary with a princess.
explanation.walkthrough: 'finishes off' trims the M from CUSTOM and the last A from DIANA, giving CUSTO + DIAN.
explanation.definitionFit: A custodian is a keeper or guardian, and a warder is a guard, so the two are synonyms.

clue.text: Firm date's arranged quickly

indicators.note: arranged means the letters are set out in a new order

parts.note: the letters of date's, the apostrophe ignored
fast means quickly

explanation.surface: A date is fixed in a hurry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'arranged' turns DATES into STEAD. 'Firm' wants to be the verb 'confirm'; it is an adjective.
explanation.definitionFit: Steadfast means unwavering and resolute, so firm in the sense of loyal and unshakeable.

clue.text: Stole stuff of judges after old yob raised limit

indicators.note: after means the fur comes after the turned word
in a down clue raised means the word is written upwards

parts.note: a Ted, a Teddy boy, was a 1950s British young tearaway
ermine is the fur used for stoles and for trimming judges' robes

explanation.surface: Something was stolen from the judges by a yob, who then lifted a limit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'raised' marks the upward turn. 'Stole' looks like a verb, but it is a fur wrap; Teddy boys were 1950s British youths in Edwardian-style clothes.
explanation.definitionFit: To determine is to fix or settle, as in limit, defining the bounds of something.

clue.text: Do so by striking international?

parts.note: you check whether a match will light by striking it; read straight, it names an international cricket fixture

explanation.definitionFit: In cricket, a five-day match between national sides is the classic international fixture.

clue.text: Tractor on tobacco fields somewhere in Canada

indicators.note: fields says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A tractor working tobacco fields in Canada.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fields' takes the run from tracTOR ON TObacco.
explanation.definitionFit: Toronto is Canada's largest city, in Ontario.

clue.text: Unhappy as to the uncomfortable position

indicators.note: unhappy letters are disturbed, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone unhappy at being put in an awkward spot.
explanation.definitionFit: Being in the hot seat is an idiom for facing awkward questions, an uncomfortable position.

clue.text: Inspiring symbol to top off dam

indicators.note: top off means the first letter of the word is removed

parts.note: to stem a flow is to dam it

explanation.surface: Instructions to finish off a dam with an inspiring emblem.
explanation.walkthrough: 'top off' removes S from STEM. 'dam' looks like a noun but is the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: A totem is an emblem or object revered as a symbol by a group.

clue.text: Switch for sale?

parts.note: a light switch could jokingly be called an ..., something that turns things on and off; straight, the phrase means available to buy

explanation.definitionFit: Goods that are available to buy are said to be on offer, an idiom.

clue.text: Caper lacks right kind of acid

indicators.note: lacks means the letter for right is missing

parts.note: a caper is a frolic

explanation.surface: A caper without the right kind of acid.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Caper' looks like the pickled bud, but it is a romp.
explanation.definitionFit: Folic acid is a B vitamin, so it is a kind of acid.

clue.text: Twisting and turning in refusal is nonsense

indicators.note: turning means the whole run of pieces is read backwards

parts.note: no is a refusal
rot is nonsense

explanation.surface: Twisting and turning on a refusal that makes no sense.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turning' reverses NO + IS + ROT. 'Twisting and turning' looks like one phrase; only the first word is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Torsion is the act of twisting something about its axis.

clue.text: Children take this in dispute

definitions.meaning: to dispute something is to take this with it, as in the idiom take ... with

explanation.surface: Children fight over this.
explanation.definitionFit: Issue means offspring, and to take issue with something is to dispute it.

clue.text: Force to have perverted love in church

indicators.note: perverted means the letters are twisted out of their order

parts.note: CE is the Church of England

explanation.surface: Forcing an act of corrupted love in a church.
explanation.walkthrough: 'perverted' rearranges LOVE + IN into VIOLEN; 'to have' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Violence is physical force used to hurt, a synonym of force.

clue.text: Crawler's not about to be put inside

indicators.note: not means the letter for about is left out

parts.note: an insect is a crawler, the apostrophe ignored
C, circa, means about

explanation.surface: A creeping person is not about to be jailed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Crawler' looks like a toady, but it is a bug; 'to be' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: To inset is to set something into something else, so to put it inside.

clue.text: End box

definitions.meaning: to put an end to a plan
to box is to strike with the fist, literally a blow to the skull

explanation.surface: End a boxing match.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means to put a stop to something, and literally it is a blow to the skull.
